findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no paper towels at the hand washing sink. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) produced paper towels. Ensure hand washing sinks are designated as hand washing sinks with signage (provided during today’s inspection), and always stocked with warm running water, soap, and paper towels. Ensure sink on the left is designated as a hand washing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the baffles of the ice machine to contain a significant amount of soil debris. Food contact surfaces should be maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of food and drinks. Inspector will return on 10/27/25. Ensure the ice machine is emptied, cleaned, and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: The right-hand faucet at the facility’s 4 part sink at the bar was observed to be only dispensing hot water. PIC stated they know to add cold water from the faucet that dispenses cold water into the sanitizer sink, and let it cool before adding sanitizer tablets. This does not account for busy periods, during which sanitizer must be available. Water heater and plumbing should be inspected and repaired by 10/27/25 by a licensed plumber to ensure cooler water is available to maintain sanitizer concentration for food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 5-104.11 System. Water shall be received from the source through the use of: (A) An APPROVED public water main; or (B) One or more of the following that shall be constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW:  (1) Nonpublic water main, water pumps, pipes, hoses, connections, and other appurtenances, (2) Water transport vehicles, or (3) Water containers. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a strainer and lemon in the handwashing sink- indicating that it’s being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- the strainer was moved. Cease this practice. Rinse sink may be emptied and used for this purpose, or the facility can use a bucket. Hand washing sinks should be used for handwashing only. A blocked hand washing sink is likely to deter hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces soiled with debris:
1) The front baffles of the ice machine
2) The holder for both soda nozzles at the bar. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) cleaned and sanitized both soda gun holders. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
- A follow up will occur on 10/15 to check the ice machine.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer compartment of the bar’s triple sink to be measuring at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia (quat). CORRECTED- PIC remade sink to a concentration of 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer solution is made at a frequency to maintain the concentration of sanitizer as recommended by the manufacturer's label. Until violation #50 is corrected, let the sanitizer water cool before adding quat tablets.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of food debris and splash on the interior sides and top of the facility’s microwave. Nonfood contact surfaces can serve as a source of contamination for ready to eat foods. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of food debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: After observing a hot water temperature at the sanitizing sink, the inspector noted the cold water faucet on the right hand side of the bar’s triple sink to not be dispensing cold water. The water in the rinse and sanitize basins was probed at 140F and 132F respectively. Skin submerged in water that is 132F+ could cause a 3rd degree burn within 15 seconds, and water that is 140F+ could cause 3rd degree burn within 5 seconds. The lack of cold water poses a safety risk to food handlers. The high water temperature also increases the rate at which sanitizer dissipates, making it harder for sanitizing solution to hold a proper concentration of 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia. A follow up will occur on 10/15/25 to ensure the water heater and plumbing have been inspected and repaired by a LICENSED plumber.
findings.citation_text: 5-104.11 System. Water shall be received from the source through the use of: (A) An APPROVED public water main; or (B) One or more of the following that shall be constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW:  (1) Nonpublic water main, water pumps, pipes, hoses, connections, and other appurtenances, (2) Water transport vehicles, or (3) Water containers. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Multiple surfaces in the kitchen were observed to contain gaps and exposed bare wood:
1) The East wall has no dry wall, and is entirely made of exposed bare wood. 
2) There is a gap between the North and East walls (next to the light switch). 
3) The West side of the bar (under the counter) contains bare wood. 
Paint or seal these areas to prevent the entry and harborage of microorganisms, which may contaminate food. Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Gaps between the wall and coving exist on the Southern wall of the kitchen. There is NO coving on either the North or West walls of the kitchen. Reseal and provide coving/ trim to these areas to prevent the growth and harborage of mold by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

The reporting agreements noted on the previous routine inspection have not been completed at this time. The PIC indicated that the printer was out of ink. Another copy of the reporting agreements given out by this department was given and another follow up was scheduled for two weeks.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

On arrival the PIC (or manager on the phone) was not aware of any paperwork acknowledging reporting responsibility for food handlers. A copy of the reporting agreements given out by SCDPH were given to the PIC and they are instructed to have signed copies ready prior to the follow up in 2 weeks.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

There was not a procedure available during this inspection for cleaning up vomit/diarrheal events in the facility. The procedure given out by SCDPH was given during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). 

On arrival the ice scoop in the ice bin at the southern end of the bar had its handle in contact with the ice. Education was conducted and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that the potential for bare hand contact with Ready-To-Eat foods (ice) is minimized/removed.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

On arrival there was a strainer in the hand sink, indicating use as a dump sink. Hand sinks should be used for no other purpose other than hand washing. The strainer was removed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda gun at the southern side of the bar has an accumulation of filth around the nozzle/sprayer connection point. The items was discussed and cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. 

There are acoustic type tiles in the men’s bathroom. These are not smooth and easily cleanable and should be switched out for tiles that ARE smooth and easily cleaned. Switch prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED. 

There is a gap between the wall and floor in the kitchen area. Provide coving/trim to seal the wall floor gap prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

The hand sink in the men’s bathroom is not sealed to the wall and currently has a gap. Seal so that there is not a gap between the wall and hand sink that is not easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

At the time of this inspection not all of the bartenders had food handler cards in their files in the office. This is the location that the PIC indicated copies should be in. Ensure that all food handlers (bartenders) have copies of current food handler certifications at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Soap dispenser in the men's room was empty. Soap was provided during inspection. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not available at the bar handwashing sink. Paper towels were provided.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the bar handsink. Handwashing signage was provided.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Murky water with debris in it was observed in the bottom of the container used for storage of ice scoop at the ice machine. Scoop and container were taken to bar to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. 

-One of the soda guns was observed soaking in soda water that had debris in it. Soda gun was to be cleaned and sanitized prior to use. Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Popcorn scoop and popping oil measuring cup were soiled from use the previous operating day. Items were taken to bar to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with non-TCS foods shall be cleaned any time contamination may have occurred. Ensure cleaning of the popcorn scoop and oil measuring cup as needed during operation and at minimum at the end of operations daily. 

-Mold was beginning to accumulate on and around the baffle in the ice machine. Cleaning and general maintenance were discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Handle of ice scoop was in direct contact with ice in the bar ice bin. Proper storage with the handle up out of ice and/or on a clean protected surface were discussed.  
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in a clean, protected location if the utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with a food that is not time/temperature control for safety food.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Plastic container used for storage of pizza slicers and other utensils had debris accumulation in the bottom. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Ensure storage containers are kept clean to protect clean utensils from potential contamination. Storage container and utensils were taken to bar to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13The pizza ovens were soiled with varying amounts of accumulation. The drip tray of the right pizza oven had some stuck on food debris. The left pizza oven had carbon accumulation on the baking tray, and the drip tray had stuck on food debris. Cleaning frequency was discussed. These surfaces are not food contact surfaces as pizza does not come in direct contact with the baking tray, and the drip tray is intended to catch any food debris that may fall during cooking. However, both parts needed to be cleaned daily dependent upon use.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of current food handler certifications were not available for all staff. At least one certification was expired, and two employee files did not contain any information pertaining to food handler certification. Owner was advised food handler certifications are required for all staff that handle food (prepare drinks, pizza, popcorn) or do anything with clean equipment and/or assist with ware washing.
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. All staff need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
